newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt gets lift from other European markets.
newsitem.headline: German debt gets lift from other European markets.

text.p: German Bunds were solidly higher in late trade, boosted by strength in other European bond markets, a trend which may well carry over into week week.
The December DTB Bund future was up 21 basis points late in the day to 98.25, off its high of the day at 98.33.
Traders said high-yielding markets elsewhere in Europe got a boost on fresh optimism about a timely start to European Monetary Union ahead of the Ecofin meeting this weekend in Dublin.
Trade, however, was light with few domestic factors emerging to give the market direction.
Traders said Bunds could climb further next week if economics and finance ministers offer optimistic comments about EMU at the weekend.
Many, however, expect the Bund future to otherwise remain in a range between 98.10 and 98.36, a previous high.

Bunds continued to outperform their U.S. counterparts with the spread widening out to 81 basis points from 80 basis points earlier in the day. That spread is near its widest level in more than two years.
The 10-year cash Bund climbed to 100.72 from 100.49 at Thursday's close to yield 6.14 percent.
Some warned, however, that the weak mark could start to undermine support for Bunds, especially against other European currencies.
Traders, however, will be reluctant to take bold positions before the September 24 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
Bunds had little reaction to German August producer prices which were unchanged from the month before.

The economic indicator schedule next week is thin with U.S. consumer confidence due out on Tuesday at 1400 GMT and final U.S. real gross domestic product data for the second quarter coming on Friday at 1230 GMT.
